general.temas: The election debate between Sánchez and Feijóo dominates the front pages, with particular attention to corruption, the economy, housing, Ceuta and the tragedies in Urda and Adamuz. Polls, the role of Junts, artificial intelligence and the summit between Trump, Putin and Xi also feature repeatedly. Only El Mundo highlights health advice for women who take the pill and use Mounjaro.
general.motivo_crispacion: The head-to-head debate features serious accusations between Sánchez and Feijóo over corruption, Ceuta and the handling of the tragedies in Urda and Adamuz. The campaign also reflects friction between Junts and the PSOE, warnings from Vox and disparaging language directed at Sanchismo. Some headlines use confrontational language that intensifies the overall tone. Stories about health, recipes and sport provide a calmer counterpoint, although they occupy less space than the electoral battle.

El País.resumen:
- The debate between Sánchez and Feijóo dominates the front page, with analysis of their claims, accusations and gestures.
- A pre-debate poll gives the PP and the right-wing bloc the lead; the Electoral Board rejects appeals from the PSOE and Vox.
- Abascal, Alvise and Junts feature in other campaign stories.
- Xi, Trump and Putin pledge to avoid nuclear war after their summit.
- The front page also covers a housing campaign linked to Blackstone and the career of writer Camila Gutiérrez.
El País.motivo_populismo: The coverage is predominantly informative, but expressions such as “they can't even stand the sight of each other,” “the first big hoax falls apart” and “pulled strings” add drama and interpretation to some headlines.
El País.sesgo: The selection focuses on the election campaign and highlights the confrontation between the candidates, scrutinizing their claims. Some headlines use interpretive or critical language, although the front page includes challenges to figures from different political positions.

El Mundo.resumen:
- Feijóo and Sánchez face off in the election debate; a poll puts the PP ahead and points to a decline for Vox.
- Puigdemont says the PSOE proposed a photo with Sánchez and rejects a possible deal with Vox.
- Trump, Putin and Xi meet in China, while Europe demands a role in negotiations over Ukraine.
- Police point to evidence of prior organization in the arrival of people swimming into Ceuta.
- Also featured are health advice on Mounjaro and contraception, Anthropic's stock market debut, and judicial and cultural news.
El Mundo.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “overwhelms him into silence,” “fanatic” and “they will remember the door being slammed in their faces for the rest of their lives” add drama and disparagement, although other headlines maintain an informative tone.
El Mundo.sesgo: The front page prioritizes political confrontation and presents the debate in a way that is favorable to Feijóo and unfavorable to Sánchez. The selection also includes critical or strongly worded headlines about Puigdemont.

ABC.resumen:
- The head-to-head debate between Sánchez and Feijóo dominates the front page, with particular attention to corruption.
- Other headlines highlight their clashes over housing, the economy, Ceuta and the rail accidents.
- The front page offers a political compass and an election poll.
- Anthropic makes its stock market debut amid doubts about artificial intelligence.
- Recipes and a reusable bottle recommendation also appear.
ABC.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “Sánchez, cornered” and “Feijóo dominates,” alongside quotes such as “You can't eat GDP,” emphasize confrontation and simplify the debate, although there is no apparent explicit appeal to the people against the elites.
ABC.sesgo: The selection and wording of the debate headlines show an approach favorable to Feijóo, who is presented as dominant, and critical of Sánchez, who is described as cornered or evasive.

Público.resumen:
- Sánchez and Feijóo feature prominently on the front page, with their messages and a vote on the debate.
- Ayuso calls for “Sanchismo” to be expelled, and the PP cancels an interview with Feijóo.
- Puigdemont joins the campaign, and the coverage addresses the arrival of AI in it.
- Several headlines deal with Andalusia and include the voice of Adelante Andalucía.
- The front page also includes pieces about victims, political allies and veteran lawmakers.
Público.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “tick,” “disposable victims” and “the art of insulting” add emotional charge and confrontation, although the first is attributed to Ayuso and other headlines are informative.
Público.sesgo: The selection highlights criticism of the PP and Junts and includes an Andalusian nationalist voice against the far right, although it also reports messages from Sánchez and Feijóo. These headlines do not allow an editorial line to be established conclusively.

OKdiario.resumen:
- The election debate between Sánchez and Feijóo dominates the front page, with emphasis on alleged mistakes by the prime minister and the PP leader's attacking stance.
- Other headlines highlight Feijóo's accusations over corruption and the economy.
- The front page offers live coverage, information on how to watch the debate and a poll on who won it.
- It also covers spending on appliances during Black Friday and the police deployment over an abandoned backpack in Barcelona.
- In sport, it covers the 75th edition of the Trofeo Ciutat de Palma and the matchup between Shelton and Alcaraz at the ATP Finals.
OKdiario.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “major slip-up,” “finishes him off,” “strips him bare” and “trolls,” together with the comparison involving stuttering, give the headlines a sensationalist and confrontational tone.
OKdiario.sesgo: The selection and wording of the debate coverage present Feijóo in an advantageous position and emphasize Sánchez's mistakes or weaknesses. The approach prioritizes confrontation and interpretation of the attacks over a balanced presentation of both candidates' positions.

opiniones.comunista:
I see the election debate turned into a duel of gestures and accusations, while the decisive question remains who controls the wealth we produce. You can't eat GDP, certainly; but it is not enough to promise tax cuts either if they weaken the public services on which the working class depends.

The story of the tenant who waited ten years for public housing and obtained it after Blackstone intervened with a Madrid official reveals an intolerable inequality of power. A basic need should not depend on the influence of a fund or an individual solution. I support a large stock of public and collective housing, democratically managed and outside the logic of speculation. Against big capital, we need guaranteed rights for everyone, not favors for a few.
opiniones.anarquista:
I listen to the election debate and wonder why we should entrust our collective life to those competing to administer it from above. Corruption cannot be solved by promises of punishment alone: as long as power is concentrated, it will be easier to use it for the benefit of a few. I prefer decisions made from below, with mandates that can be revoked and direct control by those affected.

The story of the tenant who obtained an apartment after Blackstone spoke to a public official shows, in my view, a troubling relationship between economic power and institutions. Housing should not depend on influence. I support organizing among tenants and neighbors, cooperatives and mutual aid to build alternatives. Individual freedom requires material conditions and communities capable of deciding for themselves, without masters or guardians.
opiniones.liberal:
What interests me less about the debate is who dominated the studio than one question: how much power are the candidates willing to return to citizens? When Feijóo calls for a tax cut, he points to something essential: the money a family earns should serve its own decisions first, not the priorities of politicians. But cutting taxes also requires limiting and reviewing public spending; promising everything at once is not responsible policy.

On housing, I prefer to make construction and competition easier rather than trust the state to decide for everyone. And when it comes to corruption, promises not to grant pardons are not enough: we need independent institutions and rules that prevent those in power from handing out privileges. Freedom also entails personal responsibility and respect for individual decisions, including those affecting the end of life.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
The head-to-head debate leaves one question unanswered: who is willing to truly defend Spanish sovereignty? In Ceuta, police see evidence of prior logistical planning behind the arrival of people by swimming. I want a full investigation and our borders to be firmly protected, without abandoning the dignified treatment of people. Controlling immigration is not a slogan: it is an obligation of any state that seeks to preserve its authority.

Promises of effective management or emotional appeals are not enough for me either. Corruption requires accountability and an independent judiciary, not deals of convenience between elites. And while negotiations take place with those who question national unity, I miss a clear defense of Spain as a political community and of the traditions that sustain it. We citizens deserve more than a televised duel.
opiniones.centro:
I don't need the candidates to look at each other warmly; I do need them to debate rigorously and accept that governing requires compromise. The head-to-head debate has produced serious accusations of corruption and contentious claims. The former must be investigated independently and the latter fact-checked, without turning either justice or truth into campaign weapons.

On housing, I prefer sustained reforms to miracle promises: mobilizing private investment and strengthening the public housing supply can be complementary policies. And when it comes to families' financial difficulties, neither economic growth alone nor a tax cut is an automatic answer: the services those taxes support matter too.

The apology for the rail tragedies must be accompanied by accountability and improvements. Compassion is no substitute for good management; it demands it.
